podcast.body: Released during John Frusciante's second tenure, this album continued the band's success. Frusciante's guitar work on this album, as well as on "Californication" and "Stadium Arcadium," was characterized by his professional behavior and refined sound. "la etapa de guitarra que hizo frustriante en el californicación, el baide huey o en esta parte de los rejos chílipéperes."

srcs.episode: La historia de John Frusciante: Talento, creatividad y guitarras.

podcast.body: Released in 2002, this album built upon the success of 'Californication', with much credit given to John Frusciante, who was noted for dictating most of the sounds and tones on the record. The band rehearsed for this album in a Hollywood rehearsal space called the Swing House. "The Chili's were able to build on that with the By the Way album in 2002. A lot of the credit has to go to John because he really took over with this second record, dictating pretty much all the sounds and tones."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 00's Part 3: The Return of Rock

podcast.body: Released on July 9, 2002, this album was considered by John Frusciante to be one of the best things he'd ever been involved in. Despite the era of Napster, it managed to sell close to 10 million copies globally. "The Chili Peppers with a title track of 2002's By the Way album and even in the era of Napster, that album managed to sell close to 10 million copies."
